sources.title: Azerbaijan’s Nationally Determined Contribution 3.0
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of Azerbaijan
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical climate trends, current adaptation measures and a regional vulnerability index for 2041–2069; mitigation target year 2035.
sources.methodology: Opened the 96-page NDC; reviewed regional-risk, climate, adaptation and reintegration sections.
sources.limitations: Government synthesis; index method and scenarios unspecified. Its occupation-era damage account is not independently verified.

sources.title: The Great Return
sources.organization: President of the Republic of Azerbaijan
sources.temporal_coverage: Dynamic government page on post-conflict return and reconstruction; includes return to Aghdam beginning in March 2025.
sources.methodology: Opened the government page and reviewed its coordination and Aghdam reconstruction sections.
sources.limitations: Government-reported plans and progress; dynamic page has no single publication date and does not independently evaluate outcomes.

sources.title: UNDP and ANAMA held a Side Event on Mine Action and Environmental Sustainability within COP29
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme in Azerbaijan
sources.temporal_coverage: Report of a COP29 side event held in Baku on 18 November 2024.
sources.methodology: Opened the full UNDP event report, including statements by ANAMA and UNDP representatives.
sources.limitations: Event statements; the report gives no independent soil sampling or evaluation of demining outcomes.

sources.title: Closing Ceremony Marks Completion of Project on Promoting Kahriz Rehabilitation for Climate Adaptation in Azerbaijan
sources.organization: International Organization for Migration, through United Nations in Azerbaijan
sources.temporal_coverage: Reports kahriz rehabilitation since 2000 and a project completed in March 2026.
sources.methodology: Opened the full IOM project-completion story and reviewed the reported outputs and capacity-development details.
sources.limitations: Reported project outputs are not an impact evaluation; the 20 districts are not identified and household outcomes are not disaggregated.

sources.title: 4th International Mine Action Conference: Humanitarian Demining for Urban Recovery
sources.organization: United Nations Resident Coordinator’s Office in Azerbaijan
sources.temporal_coverage: UN Resident Coordinator representative’s speech at a Baku conference on 2 September 2026; includes reported mine-action support during 2020–2025.
sources.methodology: Opened the complete speech and reviewed its return, land-release and national-capacity passages.
sources.limitations: The speech attributes figures to ANAMA and provides no calculation method or independent audit.

claims.locator: NDC 3.0, Table 2, PDF p. 22 (printed p. 23), regional climate vulnerability index
claims.paraphrase: For 2041–2069, the NDC reports highest vulnerability scores for Eastern Zangazur and Shirvan-Salyan (0.73), followed by Mil-Mugan (0.72) and Central Aran (0.68).
claims.limitations: NDC cites the 2024 NAP; index method is not stated.

claims.locator: NDC 3.0, climate profile and water resources, PDF pp. 20–22 (printed pp. 21–23)
claims.paraphrase: The NDC reports water resources fell about 15% over recent decades, irrigation uses up to 90% of water, and 200+ landslides disrupted rural communities and transport.
claims.limitations: NDC summary; underlying studies were not separately checked.

claims.locator: NDC 3.0, Table 3, PDF pp. 23–24 (printed pp. 24–25), water adaptation measures
claims.paraphrase: Listed measures include seasonal reservoirs, canal rehabilitation, drought-resistant crops, flood forecasting and early warning for irrigation and water supply.
claims.limitations: Listed measures; delivery and outcomes are unverified.

claims.locator: NDC 3.0, High-Level Summary, PDF p. 10 (printed p. 11), Garabagh and East Zangezur passage
claims.paraphrase: The NDC says reintegration of Karabakh and East Zangezur will intensify green growth through green-energy zones, smart agriculture and reforestation.
affected_groups: communities in Karabakh and East Zangezur
claims.limitations: Government-stated plan; no outcome evaluation; occupation-era damage is unverified.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The NDC explicitly links post-conflict reintegration with green growth and rehabilitation.

claims.locator: The Great Return, Coordination Headquarters and Interdepartmental Center sections
claims.paraphrase: The page lists 12 coordinating groups, including population return, mine/UXO clearance, environmental protection and efficient agricultural-land use.
claims.limitations: The page describes the coordination structure but does not evaluate its effectiveness or climate outcomes.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The page places post-conflict return and mine clearance in the same coordination system as environmental protection and agricultural-land use.

claims.locator: The Great Return, Aghdam section, return and reconstruction status
claims.paraphrase: The page says former IDP return to Aghdam began on 27 March 2025 and continues alongside demining; it lists the Khachinchay reservoir and restored roads and power infrastructure.
claims.limitations: Government page reports activities, not independently assessed access or service outcomes.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The page says IDP return in Aghdam is proceeding in parallel with demining and reconstruction.

claims.locator: UNDP COP29 event report, ANAMA and UNDP statements, 18 November 2024
claims.paraphrase: At COP29, ANAMA’s chair said detonated mines can release heavy metals and toxins into soil and air in liberated territories, creating long-term environmental risks.
claims.limitations: The article reports event statements, not environmental sampling or measured remediation results.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: ANAMA’s chair described demining as a cornerstone of climate resilience; UNDP linked clearance with safer environments and long-term recovery.

claims.locator: IOM project-completion story, opening paragraphs, 18 March 2026
claims.paraphrase: IOM reports nearly 200 kahrizes rehabilitated since 2000, benefiting over 30,000 households in 20 districts; the systems provide decentralized water in arid regions.
claims.limitations: The story does not name the 20 districts or evaluate household-level resilience outcomes.

claims.locator: IOM project-completion story, studies presented and National Water Strategy alignment
claims.paraphrase: With the State Water Resources Agency, IOM produced a cost-benefit comparison and a transparent, data-driven method to prioritize kahriz rehabilitation.
claims.limitations: The story reports studies and a selection method, not the resulting site decisions or comparative impacts.

claims.locator: IOM project-completion story, community governance and capacity-development passage
claims.paraphrase: IOM says kankans’ inherited kahriz skills risk disappearing without support and cites a capacity session in Ganja involving students from four universities.
claims.limitations: The story does not identify the universities or report whether the training produced additional kahriz practitioners.

claims.locator: UN Resident Coordinator representative’s speech, mine-action progress passage, 2 September 2026
claims.paraphrase: The speech reports 25.6% of estimated contaminated territory released for safe use, facilitating about 38,200 former IDP returns and restored activity in Karabakh and East Zangezur.
hazards: landmines and explosive remnants of war
claims.limitations: The speech attributes its figures to ANAMA and provides no calculation method or independent audit.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The speaker says mine contamination hinders safe return and farming; land release is described as enabling return and local recovery.

claims.locator: UN Resident Coordinator representative’s speech, paragraph on UN–ANAMA partnership, 2020–2025
claims.paraphrase: The speech says UNDP, UNICEF and UNHCR supported ANAMA with institutional and technical assistance, procurement and explosive-ordnance risk education during 2020–2025.
hazards: landmines and explosive remnants of war
institutions: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
claims.limitations: The speech describes assistance but does not evaluate changes in institutional performance or risk reduction.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The speech links mine-action support to safer, more resilient communities and to post-conflict recovery.

search_audit.query: Azerbaijan named economic region climate vulnerability water scarcity drought landslide primary reports
search_audit.outcome: Opened NDC 3.0 and used its named-region 2041–2069 index and climate profile. The 2024 NAP PDF was blocked; the publicly hosted World Bank CCDR was excluded because its cover marks it confidential; UNDRR PDF body was inaccessible.

search_audit.query: Azerbaijan conflict internally displaced return landmine contamination livelihoods official primary sources
search_audit.outcome: Opened the Great Return page and UN mine-action speech/event report. They identify landmines as a constraint on safe return and livelihoods; no reviewed source says climate change caused violence.

search_audit.query: Azerbaijan post-conflict return reconstruction green energy reforestation mine action climate resilience reverse pathways
search_audit.outcome: NDC 3.0 explicitly links reintegration of Karabakh and East Zangezur with green growth, smart agriculture and reforestation; UNDP reports ANAMA framing demining as climate resilience. These are stated plans/positions, not evaluated peace outcomes.

search_audit.query: Azerbaijan adaptive capacity irrigation kahriz water rehabilitation early warning mine action national capacity
search_audit.outcome: Opened NDC adaptation measures, IOM’s kahriz project-completion story and the UN Resident Coordinator speech on UN–ANAMA support; plans, reported outputs and assistance are distinguished from evaluated outcomes.

gaps: No existing AZE baseline was present in the assigned worktree.
The World Bank CCDR PDF was readable but marked on its cover as an embargoed confidential draft not for circulation; it was excluded and supplies no claims.
The 2024 National Adaptation Plan PDF was too large for the available reader, so the NDC’s reproduced index is used with its stated attribution to that plan and an index-method limitation.
The UNDRR Risk Spotlight publisher page exposed only metadata and a download prompt; its report body could not be read and no claims rely on it.

No reviewed primary report establishes that climate change caused violence in Azerbaijan. The collected evidence instead states separate climate vulnerabilities and links conflict legacies such as mines and displacement to return, land access and recovery.
The NDC’s occupation-era environmental damage statements are government assertions, not independently verified findings; NDC and official-speech figures are attributed and not independently audited.
No evaluated evidence was found on whether the listed adaptation, return, mine-action or kahriz interventions reduced climate vulnerability or improved peace outcomes.
